derivation: short_id = SHA-256(noise static public key) rendered as lowercase hex, first 16 characters -- i.e. the first 8 digest bytes. Digests computed with python hashlib.

from_public_key.name: noise_key_ab
from_public_key.note: PeerIDTests.fileTransfer_toShortNormalizesNoiseKeyToFingerprint: the short peer ID is the first 16 hex chars of SHA-256 over the RAW key bytes -- not the first 8 bytes of the key, which is the bug that test documents.

from_public_key.name: noise_key_ef
from_public_key.note: PeerIDTests.fileTransfer_truncatedRawKeyDoesNotMatchMyPeerID: contrast with the truncated form efefefefefefefef, which must NOT match.

from_public_key.name: noise_key_12
from_public_key.note: PeerIDTests.fileTransfer_shortIDProducesCorrect8ByteRoutingData: the 8-byte routing form is this hex decoded.

routing.name: short_hex_round_trip
routing.note: PeerIDTests.routingPeerRoundTrip: a 16-hex ID is already the 8 routing bytes.

routing.name: lowercased_on_construction
routing.note: PeerID lowercases in its initialiser, so 0xAA..-cased input compares equal to lowercase (PeerIDTests.equality).
